brief: Redesign the first screen of https://cerebralvalley.ai so it reads faster and feels more desirable, keeping brand and copy.

judge.reason: Dark global map proves scale but competes with headline and stats, leaving no single focal point or clear next action.

diagnosis: Face areas (FFA/STS) are silent: no human or gaze cue
Object-shape (LO) and motion (MT) areas are low: a text-first screen with no clear object silhouette
Attention drops after the first 2 s (+1.06 → +0.86): nothing to look at after the first impression
directives: Introduce a human cue: a portrait or illustrated face whose gaze points at the CTA/product (faces win attention fastest).
Add one dominant object silhouette (product shape, device frame, bold geometric hero) or a diagonal that implies motion.
Add a second discovery after the hero (a detail reveal, micro-illustration, or a strong secondary block) so interest holds past 2 s.
critique.prompt_block:

- most driven regions: places & scenes (PPA/RSC) +1.25, reward & value (OFC/vmPFC) +1.10, visual attention (IPS/FEF) +0.92; least: object shape & motion (MT/LO) -1.12, faces & people (FFA/STS) -1.47
- first-2s hook vs later: attention +1.06 → +0.86, visual drive +0.65 → +0.03
- areas the aesthetic head cites: ▲ L reward value, liking (pOFC) [aesthetic]; ▲ R salience map (IP1) [aesthetic]; ▲ object shape & motion (MT/LO) mean [attention]; ▲ object shape & motion (MT/LO) max [attention]
- diagnosis: Face areas (FFA/STS) are silent: no human or gaze cue / Object-shape (LO) and motion (MT) areas are low: a text-first screen with no clear object silhouette / Attention drops after the first 2 s (+1.06 → +0.86): nothing to look at after the first impression
- DO NEXT (highest priority first): (1) Introduce a human cue: a portrait or illustrated face whose gaze points at the CTA/product (faces win attention fastest). (2) Add one dominant object silhouette (product shape, device frame, bold geometric hero) or a diagonal that implies motion. (3) Add a second discovery after the hero (a detail reveal, micro-illustration, or a strong secondary block) so interest holds past 2 s.

judge.reason: Strong dark-system polish and instant event proposition, but the tilted card cluster and competing floating badges split focus.

diagnosis: Face areas (FFA/STS) are silent: no human or gaze cue
Place areas (PPA/RSC) dominate: the background scene swallows the message
Object-shape (LO) and motion (MT) areas are low: a text-first screen with no clear object silhouette
Reward circuit (OFC/vmPFC) is on but the appeal head is average: value is felt but what is good isn't legible
directives: Introduce a human cue: a portrait or illustrated face whose gaze points at the CTA/product (faces win attention fastest).
Simplify the environment: crop or blur the scene, put copy on a solid panel, let one subject own the frame.
Add one dominant object silhouette (product shape, device frame, bold geometric hero) or a diagonal that implies motion.
Name the value explicitly next to what the eye lands on: one benefit line + price/offer under the hero, nothing else competing.

diagnosis: Place areas (PPA/RSC) dominate: the background scene swallows the message
Face areas (FFA/STS) are silent: no human or gaze cue
Attention network (IPS/FEF) is busy: several candidates compete for the eye
Reward/value areas (OFC/vmPFC) are low: no 'I want this' signal
Attention drops after the first 2 s (+1.08 → +0.92): nothing to look at after the first impression
directives: Simplify the environment: crop or blur the scene, put copy on a solid panel, let one subject own the frame.
Introduce a human cue: a portrait or illustrated face whose gaze points at the CTA/product (faces win attention fastest).
Make a single focal point: one hero element 2–3× larger than anything else; demote secondary cards and badges.
Make the benefit concrete and desirable: show the outcome (before/after, real numbers, price or scarcity), warm highlight color on the offer, social proof near the CTA.
